subject: Biology
question: To which of the following tissues does the cell type stone cells belong?
explanation:
Stone cells (sclereids) are dead cells with thick, lignified walls. They are one of the two cell types of sclerenchyma tissue; the other is fibres.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 1.
key_points: Sclerenchyma cells: fibres and sclereids (stone cells)|Sclerenchyma gives mechanical strength

subject: Physics
question: Of the following pairs, the pair of vector quantities is,
explanation:
A vector has both magnitude and direction. Velocity and displacement are both vectors. Mass, speed, work and pressure have magnitude only, so they are scalars.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 2.
key_points: Vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum|Scalars: distance, speed, mass, work, energy, pressure

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following is the element that acts as an intrinsic semiconductor at the room temperature?
explanation:
Silicon (and germanium) are intrinsic semiconductors. Copper, aluminium and iron are metals, which are conductors.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 3.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following indicates the symbols of the elements zinc, sodium and silver respectively?
explanation:
Zinc is Zn, sodium is Na (from natrium) and silver is Ag (from argentum). Sn is tin, S is sulphur and Si is silicon.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 4.

subject: Biology
question: Select the option that correctly indicates the scientific name of plant mango.
explanation:
In binomial nomenclature the genus name starts with a capital letter, the species name is all lower case, and the whole name is printed in italics (or underlined when handwritten): Mangifera indica.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 5.
key_points: Genus: capital first letter; species: lower case|Printed in italics, underlined when handwritten

subject: Biology
topic: Structure and functions of the plant and animal cell
question: Which organelle of the cell transmits the hereditary characteristics from generation to generation?
explanation:
The nucleus contains the chromosomes (DNA), which carry the genes passed from parents to offspring.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 6.

subject: Biology
question: From which of the following structures in the ovaries of the female reproductive system an ovum is released?
explanation:
A primary follicle develops into a mature Graafian follicle, which bursts at ovulation to release the ovum. What is left becomes the corpus luteum, and later the corpus albicans.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 7.

subject: Physics
question: Cutting a yam with a well sharpened knife is easier. The reason for this is,
option_a: the ability to apply a greater force.
option_b: the ability to apply a greater pressure.
option_c: lessening the friction between the yam and the knife.
option_d: lessening the weight of the knife during sharpening.
explanation:
Pressure = force ÷ area. Sharpening makes the contact area of the edge very small, so the same force produces a much greater pressure.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 8.
key_points: Pressure = force ÷ area|Smaller area, same force: greater pressure

subject: Chemistry
question: The formula of the compound formed by the element X with oxygen is XO while the formula of the compound formed by the element Y with sodium is NaY. What is the formula of the compound formed by the combination of X and Y?
explanation:
In XO, oxygen has a valency of 2, so X has a valency of 2. In NaY, sodium has a valency of 1, so Y has a valency of 1. X (2) and Y (1) combine as XY₂.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 9.

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following is the false statement about the resistance of a metallic conductor?
option_b: It is directly proportional to the length.
option_c: It is inversely proportional to the area of cross section.
option_d: It depends on the potential difference across it.
explanation:
Resistance depends on the material, length, cross-sectional area and temperature. Changing the potential difference changes the current, not the resistance (at constant temperature).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 12.
key_points: R ∝ length|R ∝ 1 ÷ cross-sectional area|Resistance of a metal rises with temperature

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following is not a property of synthetic linear polymers?
explanation:
Synthetic polymers such as polythene are not easily broken down by microorganisms; that is why plastic waste causes pollution. They burn, resist acids and do not conduct electricity.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 14.

subject: Physics
question:
A block diagram shows some main stages of a route of transmitting electricity from an electrical power station to houses: power station → A → B → C → house. The voltage is 11 kV from the power station, 220 kV after A, 22 kV after B and 220 V after C.

What is the option that gives the transformer types indicated as A, B and C in it respectively?
explanation:
A raises 11 kV to 220 kV (step-up) for transmission with less energy loss. B lowers 220 kV to 22 kV and C lowers 22 kV to 220 V for homes, so both are step-down transformers.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 15.
key_points: High-voltage transmission reduces energy loss in the lines

subject: Biology
question: Which chamber of the human heart has the thickest walls?
explanation:
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the whole body, so it needs the thickest, most muscular wall.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 16.

subject: Chemistry
question:
The waste water released by a factory was passed through a packing of a solid substance X before emptying into the environment. The waste water entering the packing has a pH of 2.1, and the water released from it has a pH of 6.8.

Which of the following statement can be true about the waste water and X?
option_a: Waste water is acidic and X is sand.
option_b: Waste water is basic and X is sand.
option_c: Waste water is acidic and X is limestone.
option_d: Waste water is basic and X is limestone.
explanation:
pH 2.1 is strongly acidic. Limestone (calcium carbonate) neutralises the acid, raising the pH to nearly 7. Sand does not react with acids.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 17.
key_points: pH below 7: acidic; 7: neutral; above 7: basic

subject: Chemistry
question: When the cap of a bottle of soda water is opened, carbon dioxide gas bubbles are liberated. More over, carbon dioxide gas bubbles are liberated faster when a bottle of soda water kept outside a refrigerator is opened than when a bottle of soda water kept inside a refrigerator is opened. According to these observations, under which of the following conditions could it be concluded that the solubility of carbon dioxide in water increases?
explanation:
Opening the cap lowers the pressure and gas escapes, so higher pressure dissolves more gas. The warm bottle releases gas faster, so a lower temperature dissolves more gas.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 18.
key_points: Gas solubility rises with pressure|Gas solubility falls as temperature rises

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following statement is true about the image formed by a plane mirror?
option_a: The image is formed on the side of the object itself.
option_b: The size of the image depends on the size of the mirror.
option_d: The image distance depends on the geometrical shape of the mirror.
explanation:
A plane mirror forms a virtual, upright image behind the mirror, the same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and laterally inverted (left and right swapped).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 19.

subject: Physics
question: A telecommunication satellite is orbited at a height of 36 000 km from the level of the Earth. What is the time taken in seconds for a radio wave sent by a transmitting station on the Earth to reach the satellite? (Speed of radio waves in air is \(3.0\times10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).)
explanation:
Time = distance ÷ speed. The distance must be in metres: 36 000 km = \(3.6\times10^{7}\) m, so time = \(3.6\times10^{7} \div 3.0\times10^{8}\) s. Option 1 forgets to change km to m.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 20.
key_points: Time = distance ÷ speed|Convert km to m before dividing by a speed in m/s

subject: Biology
question: When a small amount of Benedict solution is added to a certain food extract and heated, no colour change occurred. When a little of dilute sulphuric acid is added to it and heated, the solution turned orange. The nutrient contained in this food extract would be,
explanation:
Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar, so it gives no colour with Benedict solution. Heating with dilute acid hydrolyses it to glucose and fructose, which are reducing sugars and give the orange-red colour.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 21.
key_points: Benedict test detects reducing sugars|Sucrose must first be hydrolysed with dilute acid

subject: Biology
question:
Consider the following characteristics possessed by a living species.
A - An organized nucleus is absent.
B - can be destroyed by antibiotics
C - can be either pathogenic or autotrophic

Of these, the characteristics owned by the organisms belonging to domain bacteria are,
explanation:
Bacteria are prokaryotes with no organised nucleus; antibiotics kill them; some cause disease (pathogenic) and some make their own food (autotrophic), for example cyanobacteria.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 22.

subject: Chemistry
question: The metals P and Q react with dilute acids liberating hydrogen gas while the metal R does not liberate hydrogen with dilute acids. P cannot displace Q from a solution of a salt of Q. What is the sequential order in which the metals P, Q and R are placed in the activity series?
explanation:
P and Q are above hydrogen and R is below it, so R is last. P cannot displace Q, so Q is more reactive than P. Order from most reactive: Q, P, R.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 23.
key_points: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its salt solution

subject: Physics
question: An arrangement named A (a transparent pen clip weighted with a lump of clay) has been introduced into a well stoppered plastic bottle filled with water so that it floats immersed. When the bottle is squeezed at its middle the arrangement A moves down the bottle. The reason for this is,
option_a: increase in the pressure of water.
option_b: increase in the weight of arrangement A.
option_c: decrease in the upthrust exerted on A.
option_d: decrease in the volume of water.
explanation:
Squeezing increases the pressure in the water, and liquids pass pressure on equally. The extra pressure squeezes the air trapped in the pen clip, more water goes in, and A sinks. The root cause is the increase in water pressure (this is a Cartesian diver).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 24.
key_points: Pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally (Pascal's principle)

subject: Physics
question:
Given below are three statements relating to motion of waves.
A - Transverse waves travel in a direction perpendicular to the direction of the vibration of particles in the medium.
B - Longitudinal waves can travel in free space (vacuum).
C - Electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in any medium.

The correct statement/s of the above is/are,
explanation:
A is correct. B is wrong: longitudinal waves such as sound need a medium. C is wrong: electromagnetic waves travel fastest in a vacuum and slower in materials such as glass or water.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 25.

subject: Chemistry
question: Of the two solutions A and B, no colour change occurred when a few drops of phenolphthalein was added to solution A. When equal volumes of solutions of A and B of equal concentration were mixed and allowed to react, an aqueous solution of C was obtained and its pH was 7. The solutions A, B and C respectively could be,
explanation:
Phenolphthalein stays colourless in acid, so A is an acid (HCl). It reacts with the base B (NaOH) in equal amounts to give the neutral salt solution C (NaCl), pH 7.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 26.
key_points: Phenolphthalein: colourless in acid, pink in base

subject: Biology
question: The carbohydrate products first formed during photosynthesis, stored temporarily in chloroplasts and translocated through the phloem respectively are,
explanation:
Glucose (a monosaccharide) is formed first, stored for a while in the chloroplast as starch (a polysaccharide), and carried through the phloem as sucrose (a disaccharide).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 27.

subject: Biology
question: The number of autosomes and the sex chromosome that can be present in a human ovum respectively are,
explanation:
An ovum is haploid: 23 chromosomes, made of 22 autosomes and one sex chromosome, which is always X in a female.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 29.
key_points: Human body cells: 44 autosomes + XX or XY|Gametes: 22 autosomes + one sex chromosome

subject: Biology
question: What is the option which correctly indicates how the curvature of the diaphragm and the volume of the thoracic cavity change when inspiration occurs in the respiratory process of a human?
option_a: curvature of the diaphragm increases; volume of the thoracic cavity increases
option_b: curvature of the diaphragm increases; volume of the thoracic cavity decreases
option_c: curvature of the diaphragm decreases; volume of the thoracic cavity increases
option_d: curvature of the diaphragm decreases; volume of the thoracic cavity decreases
explanation:
During inspiration the diaphragm muscles contract and the dome flattens (curvature decreases), so the thoracic cavity gets larger, its pressure falls, and air flows in.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 30.

subject: Physics
topic: Power and energy of electric appliances
question: The power of an electric heater is 1 000 W. The amount of electrical energy spent when this heater operated for a period of 2 hours was,
explanation:
Energy = power × time = 1 kW × 2 h = 2 kW h.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 31.
key_points: Energy (kW h) = power (kW) × time (h)

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following metals can be used for cathodic protection of iron?
explanation:
For cathodic (sacrificial) protection the metal must be more reactive than iron, so that it corrodes instead of the iron. Zinc is above iron in the activity series; Ag, Cu and Sn are below it.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 32.

subject: Physics
question: The force exerted vertically upwards on a rocket of mass m due to combustion of fuel is R. If g is the acceleration due to gravity, the acceleration with which the rocket moves is,
explanation:
The weight mg acts downwards, so the resultant upward force is R − mg. By F = ma, a = (R − mg) ÷ m.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 33.
key_points: Resultant force = ma

subject: Chemistry
question: Four gaseous hydrocarbons have these masses: A, 8.0 g of CH₄; B, 7.0 g of C₂H₄; C, 10.0 g of C₂H₆; D, 11.0 g of C₃H₈. In which of them equal number of molecules are contained? (C = 12, H = 1)
explanation:
Moles = mass ÷ molar mass: CH₄ 8 ÷ 16 = 0.5; C₂H₄ 7 ÷ 28 = 0.25; C₂H₆ 10 ÷ 30 ≈ 0.33; C₃H₈ 11 ÷ 44 = 0.25. B and D have the same number of moles, so the same number of molecules.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 34.
key_points: Equal moles contain equal numbers of molecules

subject: Chemistry
question: The boiling points of hydrogen chloride and water are -85 °C and 100 °C respectively. Which of the following statements explains the cause for this difference?
option_a: The intermolecular forces among hydrogen chloride molecules are weaker than the intermolecular forces among water molecules.
option_b: The relative molecular mass of hydrogen chloride is greater than the relative molecular mass of water.
option_c: The covalent bonds among the atoms are stronger in water than those in hydrogen chloride.
option_d: Water molecules are polar whereas hydrogen chloride molecules are non-polar.
explanation:
Boiling separates molecules from each other, so it depends on intermolecular forces, not the covalent bonds inside the molecules. Water molecules attract each other strongly (hydrogen bonds); HCl molecules attract each other more weakly. Both molecules are polar.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 36.

subject: Biology
question: Of the following, which one is the false statement?
option_a: Acid rains occur due to release of chlorofluorocarbons to the atmosphere.
option_b: Greenhouse effect is necessary to maintain life.
option_d: Oxides of nitrogen affect depletion of the ozone layer.
explanation:
Acid rain is caused by oxides of sulphur and nitrogen. Chlorofluorocarbons deplete the ozone layer; they do not cause acid rain.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 38.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following disaster conditions has the minimum influence of humans?
option_d: invasion of settlements by wild animals
explanation:
A tsunami is a natural disaster caused by undersea earthquakes. Photochemical smog, invasive plants and human–animal conflict are largely caused by human activities.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 39.

subject: Biology
question: In a traditional tank (wewa), what is the structure that prevents the erosion of the tank bund?
explanation:
The ralapanawa is a line of stones on the inner face of the bund that breaks the waves, protecting the bund from erosion. The bisokotuwa controls water released from the tank.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2024(2025) Science Paper I, question 40.

subject: Biology
question: All biomolecules carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids contain,
explanation:
All four groups of biomolecules contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Nitrogen is in proteins and nucleic acids, and phosphorus in nucleic acids, but not in all carbohydrates and lipids.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 1.

subject: Biology
topic: Structure and functions of the plant and animal cell
question: An organelle that can be seen when cheek cells are observed under the optical microscope is,
explanation:
The nucleus is large enough to be seen (especially after staining) with a light microscope. Golgi complex, mitochondria and ribosomes need an electron microscope.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 2.

subject: Physics
question: On a block of wood placed on a smooth horizontal table, horizontal, parallel forces act: 5 N and 7 N to the left, and 24 N to the right. What is the resultant force acting on the object?
explanation:
Forces to the left add to 5 + 7 = 12 N. The resultant is 24 − 12 = 12 N towards the larger side, to the right.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 3.

subject: Chemistry
question: The cause for the pain when stung by red ants is the formic acid which they apply on the sting. Application of which of the following on the sting is most effective to relieve the pain?
explanation:
A mild base neutralises the acid. Lime water (calcium hydroxide solution) is basic; vinegar is acidic and salt water and water are neutral.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 4.

subject: Biology
question: Of the following which statement is true?
option_a: All non- flowering plants are gymnosperms.
option_b: Flowering plants are also called gymnosperms.
option_c: Monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous plants are commonly referred to as angiosperms.
option_d: There are two groups of flowering plants as seed plants and seedless plants.
explanation:
Angiosperms (flowering plants) are divided into monocotyledons and dicotyledons. Non-flowering plants also include mosses and ferns, not only gymnosperms, and all flowering plants have seeds.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 5.

subject: Biology
question: A cell, a tissue and an organ in the blood circulatory system respectively are,
option_b: platelets, blood plasma and blood vessels.
explanation:
A neutrophil is a white blood cell, blood is a (connective) tissue, and blood vessels are organs. Platelets are cell fragments, plasma is not a tissue on its own, and a capillary is not a single cell.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 6.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following species contains 10 electrons, 11 protons and 12 neutrons?
explanation:
11 protons means sodium. Neutrons = 23 − 11 = 12. A Na⁺ ion has lost one electron, leaving 10 electrons.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 7.
key_points: Mass number − atomic number = number of neutrons|A positive ion has fewer electrons than protons

subject: Chemistry
question: The essential oil methyl jasmonate is the cause for the fragrance of jasmine flowers. Which following method could be used to separate methyl jasmonate industrially from jasmine flowers?
explanation:
Essential oils are extracted from plant material by steam distillation: the oil evaporates with the steam at below its own boiling point, so it is not damaged by heat.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 8.

subject: Biology
question: Which pair of following disorders is an example for the genetic disorders caused by gene mutation?
explanation:
The answer key gives albinism and thalassemia: both are caused by mutations of genes on autosomes. Haemophilia and red-green colour blindness are taught as sex-linked disorders (genes on the X chromosome).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 9.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following option correctly indicates a type of an underground stem and an example relevant to it?
explanation:
Potato is a stem tuber. Ginger is a rhizome, manioc and sweet potato are root tubers, and onion is a bulb.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 10.

subject: Physics
topic: Power and energy of electric appliances
question: A transformer is supplied with a power of 690 W from a supply of 230 V. How much is the current supplied to the coil?
explanation:
P = VI, so I = P ÷ V = 690 ÷ 230 = 3 A.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 12.
key_points: Power = voltage × current

subject: Physics
question: Which option correctly indicates the nature of radio waves and waves created on a water surface?
option_a: radio waves: transverse - mechanical; waves on a water surface: transverse - electromagnetic
option_b: radio waves: transverse - electromagnetic; waves on a water surface: transverse - mechanical
option_c: radio waves: longitudinal - mechanical; waves on a water surface: longitudinal - mechanical
option_d: radio waves: longitudinal - electromagnetic; waves on a water surface: longitudinal - electromagnetic
explanation:
Radio waves are electromagnetic waves, which are transverse. Water-surface waves need a medium (mechanical) and are treated as transverse.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 13.

subject: Chemistry
question: X, Y and Z are three successive elements in the periodic table and X is a noble gas. As which of the following species is Z most likely to exist in its compounds?
explanation:
After a noble gas X comes an alkali metal Y (group 1), then an alkaline earth metal Z (group 2). Z loses its two outer electrons and forms Z²⁺ ions.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 15.

subject: Physics
question:
Four rules relating to electromagnetism and electromagnetic induction are given below.
A - Maxwell's corkscrew rule
B - Right hand rule
C - Fleming's left hand rule
D - Fleming's right hand rule

Of these, the two rules that can be used to find the direction of the magnetic field around a conductor carrying an electric current are,
explanation:
Maxwell's corkscrew rule and the right-hand (grip) rule give the direction of the magnetic field around a current. Fleming's left-hand rule gives the force on a conductor (motors); the right-hand rule gives the induced current (generators).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 16.

subject: Physics
question:
Consider the following statements.
A - An unbalanced force does not act on an object at rest freely suspended by a string.
B - An unbalanced force acts on an object moving with a uniform velocity.
C - The force exerted on the table by an object kept at rest on a horizontal table is equal to the force exerted by the table on the object in the opposite direction.

Of the above, the true statement/statements is/are,
explanation:
A: at rest, the tension balances the weight, so there is no unbalanced force (true). B: uniform velocity means no acceleration, so no unbalanced force (false). C: action and reaction are equal and opposite (true).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 17.

subject: Biology
question: Of the following factors essential for photosynthesis, which factor cannot be tested in the school laboratory?
explanation:
Light, chlorophyll (variegated leaves) and carbon dioxide can each be removed in simple experiments. Water cannot be removed without killing the plant, because it is needed for all its life processes.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 19.

subject: Chemistry
question: The hydrocarbon with molecular formula \(\ce{C5H12}\),
option_d: forms 6 moles of water on complete combustion of one mole.
explanation:
\(\ce{C5H12}\) is an alkane (pentane), so it cannot be polymerised. Biogas is mainly methane. On combustion, its 12 hydrogen atoms form 6 molecules of water: \(\ce{C5H12 + 8O2 -> 5CO2 + 6H2O}\).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 20.

subject: Physics
question: The main reason for the easy flow of electrons across the p-n junction of a forward biased diode is,
option_b: very low value of the potential barrier.
option_c: that the depletion region is very narrow.
option_d: that the doping level is very low.
explanation:
In forward bias, the applied voltage opposes the junction's potential barrier, so the depletion region becomes very narrow and charge carriers cross it easily.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 21.

subject: Chemistry
question: u, v and w are three metals lying above hydrogen in the activity series. The method proposed by a group of students to compare their activity was taking a piece from each metal, reacting them with hydrochloric acid separately and comparing the volumes of hydrogen gas liberated within a fixed short period. Which of the following factors is not essential to be kept constant during the experiment?
option_d: acid concentration of the reaction mixture
explanation:
Over a short period, the rate depends on the surface area exposed, the temperature and the acid concentration, so these must be the same. The total mass of each piece doesn't change the early rate when the metal is in excess.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 23.

subject: Biology
question: During inspiration,
option_a: intercostal muscles and the muscles in the diaphragm relax.
option_b: intercostal muscles relax while muscles in the diaphragm contract.
option_c: intercostal muscles contract while muscles in the diaphragm relax.
option_d: intercostal muscles and muscles in the diaphragm contract.
explanation:
In inspiration the external intercostal muscles contract, lifting the ribs, and the diaphragm muscles contract, flattening it. Both make the chest cavity larger.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 24.

subject: Biology
question:
Consider the following statements about amoeba.
A - Reproduction occurs by binary fission.
B - Binary fission occurs only by mitotic division.

Of the above statements,
option_c: both statements A and B are true.
option_d: both statements A and B are false.
explanation:
Amoeba reproduces asexually by binary fission, in which the nucleus divides by mitosis, so both offspring are identical to the parent.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 25.

subject: Chemistry
question:
Two metals Q and R react as indicated by the following equations.
\(\ce{Q(s) + H2SO4(aq) -> QSO4(aq) + H2(g)}\)
\(\ce{R(s) + H2SO4(aq) -> RSO4(aq) + H2(g)}\)
\(\ce{R(s) + QSO4(aq) ->}\) no reaction

Which of the following can be Q and R respectively?
explanation:
Both react with dilute acid, so both are above hydrogen (Cu is ruled out). R cannot displace Q, so Q is more reactive than R: Q = Mg and R = Zn.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 27.

subject: Chemistry
question: A gas jar filled with a gas X was inverted and placed vertically in a beaker of water. Then, it was seen that the water level inside the gas jar rises rapidly. Gas X can be,
explanation:
The water rises quickly because the gas dissolves quickly. Ammonia is extremely soluble in water; neon and nitrogen barely dissolve, and carbon dioxide dissolves only slowly and slightly.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 28.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Heat changes associated with chemical reactions
question: In an energy level diagram, the products are at a higher energy level than the reactants. Which of the following is most likely to be the change represented by this energy level diagram?
option_c: reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid
option_d: neutralization between sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid
explanation:
Products higher than reactants means heat is absorbed: an endothermic change. Dissolving glucose absorbs heat; combustion, zinc with acid and neutralisation all release heat (exothermic).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 29.

question: The heart beat of a person whose head was injured by an accident became irregular and respiration occurred without a control. He happened to vomit also. Thus, it can be inferred that in his brain,
explanation:
The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat, breathing and vomiting. The cerebellum controls balance and coordination of movement.

subject: Physics
question: The magnetic train operated in Japan is lifted a bit up above the rails after it acquires an adequate speed and made to run forward. What is the main advantage obtained by this modern technological strategy?
option_b: minimizing the wear of the rails
option_c: minimizing air resistance acting on the train
option_d: running the train under minimal friction
explanation:
Lifting the train off the rails removes the contact between wheels and rails, so the main gain is very low friction, allowing very high speeds.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 31.

subject: Chemistry
question:
Two reactions used to prepare the gases H₂ and CO₂ in the laboratory are given below.
\(\ce{Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2}\)
\(\ce{CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2}\)

What is the mass of \(\ce{CaCO3}\) that should be reacted to obtain an amount of moles of \(\ce{CO2}\) gas which is equal to the maximum amount of moles of \(\ce{H2}\) gas obtainable from 32 g of zinc (Zn)? (H = 1; C = 12; O = 16; Ca = 40; Zn = 64)
explanation:
32 g Zn ÷ 64 = 0.5 mol Zn, giving 0.5 mol \(\ce{H2}\). 0.5 mol \(\ce{CO2}\) needs 0.5 mol \(\ce{CaCO3}\) (molar mass 100 g/mol), which is 50 g.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 32.
key_points: Moles = mass ÷ molar mass|Use the mole ratio in the balanced equation

subject: Chemistry
question: In the form of a thin layer, metal X is applied on the iron sheet A and metal Y is applied on the iron sheet B. A small scratch was made at the centre of both sheets. Later, rusting has spread rapidly on A, but B has not been subjected to a considerable damage. The metals X and Y respectively can be,
explanation:
Once scratched, a less reactive coating (tin) makes iron rust faster, because iron becomes the metal that corrodes. A more reactive coating (zinc, galvanising) corrodes instead of the iron, protecting it.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 33.

subject: Physics
question: 600 g of water at temperature 80°C were added to a vessel containing 200 g of water at 0°C. What is the final temperature of the mixture? (specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹; assume that the vessel does not absorb heat.)
explanation:
Heat lost = heat gained: 0.6 × 4200 × (80 − θ) = 0.2 × 4200 × (θ − 0). So 3(80 − θ) = θ, 240 = 4θ, θ = 60 °C.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 34.
key_points: Heat = mass × specific heat capacity × temperature change|Heat lost by hot = heat gained by cold

subject: Physics
question: The areas of cross section of the pistons of a hydraulic jack are x m² and 4x m². How much is the force exerted on the larger piston when a force of 50 N is applied on the smaller piston?
explanation:
The pressure is the same on both pistons: 50 ÷ x = F ÷ 4x, so F = 4 × 50 = 200 N.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 35.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is a disease which cannot be either controlled or prevented by changing the life style?
explanation:
Haemophilia is an inherited (genetic) disorder, so lifestyle cannot prevent it. Diabetes, gastritis and chronic kidney disease are linked to diet, habits and environment.

question: In which phase of the growth curve of population does the number of organisms in the population reach its carrying capacity?
explanation:

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following statements is true about the ecological pyramids?
option_b: In a biomass pyramid, omnivores can exist only as secondary consumers.
option_c: Heavy metals accumulate most in the highest level of a biomass pyramid.
option_d: Biomagnification is the incorporation of a higher amount of energy in the higher trophic levels of an energy pyramid.
explanation:
Heavy metals are not broken down or excreted, so they concentrate up the food chain (biomagnification) and are highest in the top consumers. Number pyramids can be inverted (for example a tree with many insects).

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 39.

subject: Biology
question:
As a student says, nitrogenous nutrients in a soil decrease after a flood due to following reasons.
A - occurrence of denitrification
B - percolation deeper into soil (leaching)
C - getting washed away from the surface soil
D - decomposition of organic matter

Of these only,
option_a: A, B and C are true.
option_b: A, B and D are true.
option_c: A, C and D are true.
option_d: B, C and D are true.
explanation:
Waterlogged soil lacks oxygen, which favours denitrifying bacteria (A); water carries nitrates down (B) and washes away the surface soil (C). Decomposing organic matter adds nitrogen nutrients rather than removing them.

Source: G.C.E. O/L 2025(2026) Science Paper I, question 40.
